 SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway EPG system remotely through API calls.

3 Introduction
 Internet acquiring is used to sell goods and services via the public Internet, allowing
 customers to use their regular bank cards to ma ke purchases. A merchant planning to
 sell goods or services via the Internet must ensure the security of the payments being
 processed by ta king the following measures:

 · Key data (such as personal data and bank cards details) must be transferred via a
    secure SS  ( L or TLS) connection.
 · Information about the current payment (amount, currency, or description of the order)
    and the result of the payment must be protected from and not be accessed by
    intruders.

 · Before the payment is made, the customer’s card parameters (for example, the
    expiration date, cardholder name and so on should be checked.      )
 The 3-D Secure protocol is used to provide an additional security layer. The major
 payments networks have introduced their own services based on the 3-D Secure
 protocol, for example, Mastercard has “Mastercard Identity Check” and Visa has “Visa
 Secure”.

 The SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway is used as a technology platform. It
 enables a merchant to perform the necessary safety procedures without the need to
 significantly restructure their Internet store site and existing business processes. EPG
 supports the following operations:

 · P2P transactions
 · Recurring payments

3.3 Application version numbering policy
 SmartVista products are certified in accordance with PC I SSF PC I Software Security                 (
 Framework) standards. To enable you to understand the PCI SSF version with which the
 product you use complies, product versions are numbered in a standard way:

 2.2.25.<Group code>-<Component code><Release number>.<Fix number>, where:
 · 2 — general version of SmartVista that complies with Secure SLC Standard and
    Program Guide v.1.1 and the Secure Software Standard and Program Guide v.1.1

 · 2 — general version of e-commerce products that complies with Secure SLC Standard
    and Program Guide v.1.1 and the Secure Software Standard and Program Guide v.1.1

 · 25 — major update version of E-commerce Payment Gateway (EPG) that complies with
                  L
    Secure S C Standard and Program Guide v.1.1 and the Secure Software Standard and
    Program Guide v.1.1

 · <Group code> — internal code of a BPC group
 · <Component code> — code of the e-commerce application
 · <Release number> — number of the release of the e-commerce application

5 Request structure
 The examples of requests provided in this document include the query and J SON body.
 The J SON body parameters are in braces                         ({), for example:
 https://<host:port>/epg/rest/p2p/register.do?userName=test_api&password=1
 {
     "amount": 1,
     "currency": "840",
     "returnUrl": "http://127.0.0.1/cart.html",
     "orderNumber": "88878890887535756777"
 }

 where the following is the query:

 https://<host:port>/epg/rest/p2p/register.do?userName=test_api&password=1

 and the following is the J SON body:

 {
       "amount": 1,
       "currency": "840",
       "returnUrl": "http://127.0.0.1/cart.html",
       "orderNumber": "88878890887535756777"
 }

6 REST API
 Interactions between the merchant and the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway
 are implemented as HTTP requests with GET or POST methods to specific URLs. These are
 separate for each individual request type.

 IMPORTANT: It is highly recommended that you use the POST method and send
 parameters of a request in the request body with the content type application x-www-form-                    /
 URL-encoded if the other content type is not explicitly required by a specific API
 according to its description. If the GET method is used, sensitive request parameters may
 be undesirably stored in logs due to the HTTP protocol peculiarities and the logging
 settings of the network infrastructure components. However, all request examples are
 provided with the GET structure for the sa ke of clearer visual illustration.

 The parameters used in the interactions are sent as parameters of GET or POST requests                               ;
 their values must be           URL-encoded.
 The result of processing a request returns as a JSON ob j ect, for example:

 {"errorCode":"12","errorMessage":"Empty amount"}

 For authorization purposes, each request must include the login and password of the
 user who manages merchants and were generated during the user’s registration. The
 values are sent as the following parameters:


 Name                                                                              Type                 Mandatory
 userName                                                                          AN 1..100            Yes
 Login of the user generated during registration.
 password                                                                          String               Yes
 Password of the user generated during registration.

 application/json, text/javascript, */*;

 Either one-phase or two-phase payment schemes may be used :

 · One-phase payment — a payment for goods or services executed through the Internet
   with the use of a bank card. It is executed as one action that does not require
   additional confirmation.

 · Two-phase payment — a payment for goods or services executed through the Internet
   with the use of a bank card and requiring additional confirmation. The two-phase
   mechanism splits the process into checking whether the card is capable of paying




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                     |       25
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




  (authorization) and debiting the money from the account (financial confirmation).
  During the first step of a two-phase payment, the bank card paying capacity is checked
  and money on the customer’s account are put on hold. The second step is a
  confirmation of the funds transfer.

6.1 Order registration request
  Depending on whether one-phase or two-phase payments are used, one of the following
  methods is used to register an order:

  · register.do — for one-phase payments
  · registerPreAuth.do — for two-phase payments

  These requests are designed to register orders in the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment
  Gateway and have the same set of parameters.


  Request parameters
  Name                                                                              Type          Mandatory
  userName                                                                          AN 1..100     Yes
  Login of the API user on whose behalf requests are processed for a specific merchant.
  password                                                                          String        Yes
  User’s password.
  orderNumber                                                                       AN 1..32      No

  Number (identifier) of the order in the merchant’s online store system. It is unique for
  every store in the system and is generated on the order registration.

  If the Require system to generate order numbers permission is enabled for the merchant,
  the order number is generated automatically. Otherwise, the order number data is sent
  in the API.


  amount                                                                            N 1..12       Yes
  Order amount in the minor denomination (for example, cents).

  currency                                                                          N3            No

  Payment currency code in the ISO 4217 format.

  If the currency parameter in the request is not specified, the default currency code is
  used.


  returnUrl                                                                         ANS 1..2000   No

  URL to which the customer is redirected after a successful payment.
  description                                                                       ANS 1..600    No

  Free form description of the order.

recurrenceType                                                                    String            Yes for recurring
                                                                                                    payments


Way in which subsequent recurring payments are processed:
· AUTO — for automatic handling of payments scheduled on the EPG side.
· MANUAL — for manual processing of recurring payments scheduled on the merchant
   side.


For recurring payments, this parameter is used to schedule the next payment (if AUTO is
selected ).

For installment payments, the parameter is used to schedule the next payment (if AUTO is
selected ) and check if the merchant is sending the request at the correct time (if MANUAL
is selected ).

When the next payment date comes, the system sends an AUTO payment request
according to the schedule, and the merchant sends a MANUAL payment request.

 EPG checks whether the payment date is correct. If it is not, the request is rej ected and
the merchant is warned that that it is not time for the payment either too early or too    (
      )
late . For the late payments, an updated installment payment date                              (recurrenceEndDate
                                     )
and recurrenceFrequency must be provided before a new payment can be made. If
recurrenceType = MANUAL, the merchant can initiate a recurrentPayment.do request any
time regardless of the date specified by the recurrenceFrequency parameter. The system
does not validate whether the payment date matches the scheduled installment plan.

The recurrenceType parameter is mandatory to register a recurring or installment
payment.

The recurrenceType parameter is not used in the registerPreAuth.do method.


recurrenceFrequency                                                               String            For MANUAL: No
                                                                                                    For AUTO: Yes

This pa rameter is mandatory for AUTO installments and recurring payments and is
ignored for MANUAL installments and recurring payments.

For information about configuring this parameter, see Specifying

Note: Either all three parameters are required or none of them: installmentTotalAmount,
installmentSingleAmount, and installmentNumber. The recurrenceEndDate and
recurrenceFequency parameters are required for installments.

the merchant.

6.4 No-Show payment request
 The noShow.do request is used to complete a no-show transaction. No-show is a fee billed
 by a merchant in accordance with the merchant’s service policy when the cardholder
 fails to cancel a reservation within the time frame disclosed at the time of the booking.
 No-show only works if card credentials were saved when the card was registered or
 when the card binding was created.

 The noShow.do transactions are sent when the order is in the Approved state
 (preauthorizations). The No Show request amount is not limited by the


 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                      |   46
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




Toleranceparameters set for deposits or incremental authorizations. The order state is
changed to Deposited.

Refunds and reversals for the No-Show transactions are created in a standard way,

Merchant options
To be able to execute this method, the merchant must have the Can use No-Show payments
permission enabled.

6.6 Multiple completion request
 The partialDeposit.do request is used to partially deposit the preauthorized amount in
 the scenario of multiple completions for two-phase payments.

 The partialDeposit.do request is used during non-final completions. To finalize payment
 and release remaining funds from the cardholder’s account, the value of field 47.177
 (Multiple Completion Indicator) must be 2 — multiple completion transaction, final
 completion.
 Users can perform this request if they have the relevant permission in the system. A
 merchant must have at least one user with the Use Merchant API and Partial deposit
 allowed permissions. For more information, see “Main information tab” in the
 “Merchants” section and the “Creating a user” section of the SmartVista E-Commerce
 Payment Gateway: User Guide.

6.7 Payment request
 The paymentorder.do method is used for a payment request. The payment card data is
 validated in accordance with the table below:

Transaction Data block
A single signed data block is used to transfer all original transaction data fields to and
from a PC I     DSS merchant, instead of multiple separate fields.
An RSA key pair with CertificateType.TRANSACTION_DATA_SIGNATURE must be generated for
the merchant.

The block includes the following:


Header
Field                                   Description
alg                                     Algorithm      (RS256).
kid                                     ID of the corresponding record in the key_mgmt_certificate
                                        table.


typ                                     Header type (JOSE).

merchantLogin                           Login of the merchant.
Payload
Field                                   Description
mdOrder                                 This field is reserved for future use.


transDate                               This field is reserved for future use.


networkReferenceData Network reference data returned from the authorization host.
transactionDataElemen Data elements of the authorization request.
ts
isSsl                                   Specifies whether 3           DS2 authentication was not performed for
                                        the transaction.

                                        transactions).


acsTransId                              Transaction I      D in ACS (only for 3DS2 transactions).
initTransactionDate                     Initiating transaction date (only for 3DS2 transactions).

version                                 Constant value of 1. This field is reserved for future use.


panSalt                                                                                    (
                                        Base64-encoded 16 bytes random salt the resulting string
                                                                                               ;
                                        will be approximately 24 character long from SecureRandom .          )

S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




Field                                   Description

The block validation fails if:

· The field is missing for MIT requests with recurringPaymentManagedByMerchant=true or
  bindingManagedByMerchant=true.
· A different merchantLogin is used.
· The key provided in the JWS header cannot be found for the current merchant.
· Signature validation fails (both technical and not errors).

If 3-D Secure is required to perform a payment, then after the response to the payment
request has been received, the merchant must redirect the customer to ACS.

To redirect the customer to ACS, the merchant must perform a redirection to the address
specified in the acsUrl parameter with the body of the request. The request must be in
the POST format.




Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                    |    64
  S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




  Depending on the integration scheme, after passing the authentication on ACS, the
  customer is redirected to the merchant or to EPG. The processes of payment completion
  for each of these cases are listed below.

  Return to the payment gate from ACS
  In the classic scheme, the issuing bank’s ACS authenticates the cardholder and redirects
  them to the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway sending the Payer Authentication
  Response (PARes). If the cardholder was authorized by ACS successfully, EPG authorizes
  the order. Having received PARes, EPG processes the authentication results and sends
  the authorization request to the acquirer’s system.

  Return to the merchant from ACS using Finish 3DS
  The scheme uses an additional method, Finish 3                           DS. In this scheme, the issuing bank’s
  ACS authenticates a cardholder and redirects the cardholder to the merchant. The
  PARes from ACS is sent to the merchant. The merchant then transfers it to EPG via the
  finish3dsPayment.do method.

authentication. It is used in 3-             D Secure 1.
This parameter is not used in payments that do not require additional authentication on
the issuing bank’s ACS.


cReq                                                                              AN..512         Conditional


Challenge Request message. EMV 3-                       D Secure message sent by the 3DS SDK or 3DS
Server where additional information is sent from the cardholder to the ACS to support
the authentication process. It must be present for 3-                          D Secure 2 if a cardholder
challenge is required.


For UPOP payments, purchaseUpopRedirect.do is automatically executed after a
successful execution of paymentotherway.do. The purchaseUpopRedirect.do method
generates and sends a page for the cardholder’s purchase submission.

6.11 Finish3dsPayment request
 The finish3dsPayment.do request is used as a final step of the cardholder authentication
 with 3   DS. It is used to transfer data to the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway.
 The issuing bank’s ACS authenticates a cardholder and redirects the cardholder to the
 merchant. The C Res            (3DS2) or PARes (3DS1) from ACS is sent to the merchant. The
 merchant then transfers it to the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway via the
 finish3dsPayment.do method.

6.13 Account update request
 The updateAccount.do method is used to request card data for the specified merchant and
 the card from the database. After receiving a response:

 · All binding and recurring data for all merchants in EPG is updated if the card and the
   merchant were found in the database.

 · If a card and/or a merchant is not registered in EPG, the error is returned and the
   account data is not updated.


 The updateAllAccounts.do method requests data on all cards for the specified merchant.

 The updateAccount.do and updateAllAccounts methods are used to update account
 information for bindings and recurring payments if the updateAccount parameter in the
 Recurring payment request
                                           166

                                                 is enabled.

6.14 Order reversal request

                                                   (
  available within a limited period specified by the bank after a payment has been   )
  executed.

  The reversal transaction may be performed only once for a payment. If a reversal request
  results in an error, the next try will fail.

  bank to perform reversals. Users must have the relevant permissions to perform the
  reversal request.

6.15 Partial reversal request
  The reversePartial.do request is used if it is necessary to ad j ust a portion of the original
  transaction amount. This functionality is available within a limited period specified by              (
               )
  the bank after a transaction has been executed. Two or more consecutive partial
  reversals per one transaction cannot be performed.

  The partial reversal amount must be greater than zero and less than the original
  transaction amount.

  The order status does not change after partial reversal has been completed.

  Reversals are available to a merchant only if the merchant has an agreement with its
  bank to perform reversals. Users must have the relevant permissions to perform a partial
  reversal request.

6.17 Refund request
 A refund.do request is used to refund deposited money.

 This request returns the funds paid for the order back to the customer. The request
 results in an error if the customer was not charged. The request allows multiple refunds,
 but their total amount cannot exceed the amount that was deposited from the customer’s
 account as a result of the order.

 A merchant’s user must have a corresponding permission in the system to perform a
 refund request.

  line , and \n line brea k .        )

6.23 Request for payments statistics for a period
  The getLastOrdersForMerchants.do method is used to get the payment statistics for a
  specified period. The method returns a list of order descriptions, where each description
  represents an extended order status that can be received by executing the
  getOrderStatusExtended.do request (see Extended order status request                               ) for a specific
                                                                                                92




  order.


  Request parameters
  Name                                                                              Type             Mandatory
  userName                                                                          AN 1..100        Yes
  Login of the API user on whose behalf requests are processed for a specific merchant.
  password                                                                          String           Yes
  User’s password.
  language                                                                          A2               No

  Language code in the ISO 639-1 format. If it is unspecified, SmartVista E-Commerce
  Payment Gateway uses the default language from the merchant settings.

  Error messages are also returned in this language.


  page                                                                              N                No

  When processing the request, a list is formed that is broken down into pages (with the
                                                                             )
  number of records on each page of the same size . A page with the number that was
  specified in the page parameter is returned in the response. The pages numbering
  starts from 0. If the parameter is not specified, a page with the number 0 is returned.


  size                                                                              N..3             Yes
  Number of elements on a page. The maximum value is 200.

  from                                                                                               Yes
  Date and time when the period of collecting orders starts, in the following format
  YYYYMMDDHHmm.

  to                                                                                                 Yes
  Date and time when the period of collecting orders ends, in the following format
  YYYYMMDDHHmmss.
  transactionStates[]                                                               A..9             Yes

report. If there are several values, they are separated by commas. The following values
are available:

· CREATED
· APPROVED
· DEPOSITED
· DECLINED
· REVERSED
· REFUNDED

merchants[]                                                                       ANS              Yes
List of logins of the merchant whose transactions are included in the report. If there are
several values, they are separated by commas.

Leave this field empty to get the list of reports on all the available merchants (child
merchants and merchants specified in the settings of the user).


searchByCreatedDate                                                               Boolean          No

Specifies whether the creation date is used to search for orders:

· true — a search for orders that have the creation date that falls into the specified
   period.

· false — a search for orders that have the payment date that falls into the specified
  period (thus, orders in the CREATED or DECLINED status cannot be present in the report).
   This is the default value.

6.28 Request for payment with Mastercard SCoF
token
 The epg/api/v1/mastercard/scof/payment/decrypted method is used to transfer decrypted
 payment data tokenized by Mastercard SCoF.


 System settings
 On the Administration > System settings page of the EPG administration portal the
                                                      (
 following setting must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
 Installation and Configuration Guide):
  wallets.token.range.validation.enabled

  Description                             Parameter that enables validating a token against an
                                          account ranges stored in the database. The token must fit in
                                          one of the ranges marked as tokenized in the       (


 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                            |   140
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




wallets.token.range.validation.enabled

                                         ACCOUNT_RANGE_INFO table, the TOKEN = 1 column). Possible
                                         values:

                                         · true — the token is validated.
                                         · false — the token is not validated. This is default value.


Merchant options
To be able to execute this method, the merchant must have the Can pay with Mastercard
SCoF by token decrypted permission enabled.

Acquirer options
The acquirer via which the payment is performed must have the Mastercard SCoF payment
way enabled in the acquirer configuration.


User permissions
The user must have the following permission enabled on the Administration                            > Users page
(see “Adding a group of permissions” and “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-Commerce
Payment Gateway: User Guide):

Permission                                                                        Action type   Level

User can process Mastercard SCoF token payments for the merchant.
This request is authenticated with the userName and password parameters that must be
transferred.

                                                       (
 following setting must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
 Installation and Configuration Guide):
  fee.service.enabled

  Description                              Enables the fee service that is used to calculate a fee.

6.34 Transaction acknowledgment request
 The /epg/rest/public/acknowledgeTransaction.do method is used to acknowledge a
 transaction after a payment is completed. A transaction acknowledgement is required if
 the transaction.acknowledgement.enabled option is enabled in the EPG configuration.
 Without the acknowledgement, the transaction is set for reversal. The acknowledgement
 request must be sent within the period specified in the EPG configuration. For more
 information, see the “Transaction acknowledgement settings” section in SmartVista E-
 Commerce Payment Gateway: Installation and Configuration Guide.

6.36 Recurring payments
 This section contains the description of API methods used for recurring payments. A
 recurring payment is a payment model where the customers authorize the merchant to pull
 funds from their accounts automatically at regular intervals for the goods and services
 provided to them on an ongoing basis.

 Recurring payments are performed as follows:
 1. The first recurring payment is registered by the register.do                             28
                                                                                                  request sent by a
      merchant.

      This request contains necessary recurring parameters such as recurrenceType,
      recurrenceFrequency, recurrenceStartDate, recurrenceEndDate.
 2. EPG registers the order and sends a response with recurrenceId.
 3. The merchant sends the paymentorder.do request with card data to process the first
      recurring transaction.

 4. The second and subsequent recurring payments are made using the
    recurringPayment.do    method. If recurenceType=MANUAL, the merchant may initiate a
                                       166




    recurrentPayment.do request any time regardless of the date specified by the
    recurrenceFrequency parameter. The system does not validate whether the payment
      date matches the scheduled installment plan.


 EPG also enables users to perform the following actions:

 · Create templates for recurring payments using the
   createRecurringTemplateNoPayment.do   method
                                                            177




 · Get a list of transactions processed for a specific recurring payment using the
   getRecurrentReport      method
                                 175




 · Update information about a recurring payment the using the updateRecurrent.do                                  168




    method




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                           |   165
  S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




  · Get information about a specific recurring payment using the getRecurrentDetails                        171




    method



6.36.1 Recurring payment request
  The recurringPayment.do method processes subsequent recurring payments based on a
  respective recurrenceId generated on the first payment registration see the                   (
  description
                    28
                         of register.do .    )
  Note: This operation is only used for manual recurring payments.
  To be able to execute this method, a merchant must have the Recurrent payments allowed
  permission enabled. A merchant must have at least one user with the Use Merchant API
  and Recurrent payment allowed permissions. For more information, see       “Main information
      ”
  tab in the      “Merchants” section and the “Creating a user” section of the SmartVista E-
  Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide.
  Note: A recurring payment must be associated with an active acquirer. If a recurring
  payment is associated with an acquirer that has been deleted or deactivated, the
  default acquirer is set for the next recurring payment.

6.37.2 Request for Apple Pay payments
  Apple Pay payments are processed using the /api/v1/applepay/payment method.

  In general, a payment is processed as follows:
  1. On the merchant website, a customer places an order. The merchant server performs
     a range of checks for the availability of Apple Pay to the customer, and, depending on
      the result, offers the customer the ability to use the Apple Pay payment option or to set
      up Apple Pay.

  2. After the customer has used Apple Pay, the merchant server starts a payment session
     with the Apple server during which it exchanges the payment data and validates the
     payment request with the Apple server. After the customer is authenticated by Touch
     ID or Face ID, the merchant server encrypts the payment data and sends it to the
     Apple server to sign with the open key of the merchant stored on that server.

  3. When the merchant server receives the signed data, it encrypts the data (it creates a
      payment token, according to the Apple terminology) and sends it to EPG, which
                                                                       L (
      decrypts it and passes the request to the O TP online transaction processing system               )
      for the further routing to an international payments network.


  The following forms of the request are used :

  · A request with encrypted payment data (authenticated or anonymous)
  · A request with decrypted data
  · A request with Base64 encrypted payment data
  · A request for a session object

  To enable Apple Pay payments in EPG, the following settings are required :

  System settings




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                              |   189
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




On the Administration > System settings page of the EPG administration portal the
                                                       (
following settings must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
Installation and Configuration Guide):
applepay.signature.verify

Description                              Parameter that defines whether to verify the Apple Pay
                                         certificate signature.

                                         The default value is true.


secureKeystorePassword

Description                              Parameter that enables validating a token against an
                                         account ranges stored in the database. The token must fit in
                                         one of the ranges marked as tokenized in the           (
                                         ACCOUNT_RANGE_INFO table, specifically the TOKEN=1 column).
                                         Possible values:

                                         · true — the token is validated.
                                         · false — the token is not validated This is the default value.

6.37.2.1 Request for Apple Pay payment with encrypted data
  The /api/v1/applepay/payment/encrypted or /api/v1/applepay/payment/encrypted-anonymous
  method is used to transfer encrypted data for an Apple Pay payment.

  and password parameters are required for authentication.

6.37.2.3 Request for Apple Pay payment with decrypted token
  The /api/v1/applepay/token/decrypt method is used to transfer decrypted data for an
  Apple Pay payment.

  EPG receives a request with the Base64 encrypted payment data, decodes the payment
  data and returns a response with the decrypted payment data

  This request is not authenticated. The merchant login the                         (         merchant parameter) is used
  to perform all the checks.

   Note: To enable anonymous data processing, the Anonymous access allowed setting must
   be enabled on the Di g ital wallets > Goog lePay tab of the merchant settings (see
   “Creating a merchant” in SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).
  Request parameters
   Name                                                                              Type                   Mandatory
   merchant                                                                          AN 1..100              Yes
   Merchant login to access EPG.

   paymentToken                                                                                             Yes
   Base64 encrypted payment data. For the format of paymentToken, see Payment Token                     “
   Format Reference” (the version dated 2017-09-19) at the following link to Apple
   documentation:
   https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/PassKit/Reference/Payment
   TokenJ SON/PaymentTokenJ SON.html.


   customerBillingAddress[]                                                          Not applicable         No

   Address associated with the customer’s bank account and used to send bills. For the
                                                                                                            525

   description of the parameters, see customerBillingAddress parameters                                           .



  Response parameters
   Name                                                                              Type                   Mandatory
   applicationPrimaryAccountNumber                                                   N 12..19               Yes
   Account number that has been used for the payment.


   applicationExpirationDate                                                                                Yes
                                                                                     YYYYMMDD
   Expiration date.




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                        | 204
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




Name                                                                              Type        Mandatory

Transaction amount.

6.37.3 Request for Google Pay payments
  EPG offers multiple implementation options for Google Pay that allows merchants to
  submit payment requests with payment data in various formats to initiate a Google Pay
  transaction.
  Additionally, if the payment page is implemented on the merchant s side, the merchant      '
  can integrate directly with Google Pay and submit the payment data to EPG for
  authorization. If a hosted payment page is used, EPG integrates with Google Pay and
  processes the payment on behalf of the merchant.

  EPG also provides the APIs used to decrypt tokens. These are non-payment APIs that do
  not submit a payment request to SVFE.




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                   | 209
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface

                           Example: =^[a-zA-Z0-9\S\s]+$

Description                Parameter that enables the use of data decryption only for an offline
                           key uploaded to EPG.
                           · true — a key for the signature validation is fetched from the
                                                     (
                              database only uploaded by the merchant user on the Administration
                              > Common Certificates page on the EPG administration portal, see
                              SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).
                           · false — a key is fetched from the Google server. If the server cannot
                              be reached, the offline key is searched in the database.

                           The default value is false. A value of true is recommended for the
                           production mode.

                            Note: Changing the parameter value does not require the application
                            restart to apply the changes. Cash is renewed when uploading a new
                            key or deleting an old key.

6.37.3.1.2 Request for Google Pay payment with an encrypted token as JSON
   A Google Pay transaction that uses encrypted payment data (DPAN) transfers a token
   (paymentToken) to EPG. The payment token is a JSON structure that contains Google Pay
   keys (intermediateSigningKey[] , signedMessage) and an encrypted token (PAN/DPAN,
                                                  535




   and other). Once the EPG receives the /api/v1/googlepay/payment/encrypted request, it
   decrypts the token using private keys.

   The /api/v1/googlepay/payment/encrypted request is authenticated, in this case the
   userName and password parameters are required for authentication.

   Note: The anonymous request similar to the /api/v1/googlepay/payment/encrypted
   request can be sent from the hosted payment page without the username and password
                     (
   parameters see Request for Google Pay payment with encrypted token as J SON via
   hosted payment page

                                           ).

6.37.3.1.3 Request for Google Pay Payment with Base64-encoded encrypted token
   The /api/v1/googlepay/encodedtoken/encrypted request is used to process payments using
   a Google-signed and encrypted payment method token. Additionally, the payment token
   is in Base-64 encoding.

   Within the transaction flow, EPG verifies and decrypts the token (Google Pay payment
   data as a Base64 encoded string, which contains the payment token ob j ect).

   Note: The anonymous request similar to the /api/v1/googlepay/encodedtoken/encrypted
   request can be sent from the hosted payment page without the username and password
                     (

                                      (intermediateSigningKey[], signedMessage) and an

6.37.3.3 Merchant-side Google Pay implementation: non-payment APIs
   The following APIs are provided to decrypt payment token data without initiating a
   payment request for authorization to SVFE:

   · Request for Google Pay data decryption from encrypted token as JSON
                                                                                                     233




   · Request for Google Pay data decryption from Base64 encoded encrypted token
                                                                                                           235




6.37.3.3.1 Request for Google Pay data decryption from encrypted token as JSON
   This request contains the Google-signed and encrypted payment method token. This API
   endpoint is designed to decrypt the payment token to retrieve the underlying payment
   data.

6.37.4 Request for Samsung Pay payments
  Samsung Pay payments are processed using the /api/v1/samsungpay/payment method.

  The following forms of the request are used :

  · A request with encrypted payment data (authenticated or anonymous)
  · A request with decrypted data
  · A request with Base64 encrypted payment data

  To enable Samsung Pay payments in EPG, the following settings are required :

  System settings
  On the Administration > System settings page of the EPG administration portal, the
                                                       (
  following setting must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
  Installation and Configuration Guide):




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                               | 2 38
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




wallets.token.range.validation.enabled

Description                Enables the validation of a token against an account ranges stored in
                           the database. The token must fit in one of the ranges marked as
                                           (
                           tokenized in the ACCOUNT_RANGE_INFO table, specifically the TOKEN=1
                                   )
                           column . Possible values:

                           · true — the token is validated.
                           · false — the token is not validated. This is the default value.


Merchant options
The merchant must have the following options enabled in the                                Main information tab of the
merchant settings of the Administration                    > Merchants page (see "Creating a merchant" in
SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide):

Permission                        Description
Can pay with                      Merchant is allowed to process payments with Samsung Pay.
Samsung Pay
Can pay with                      Merchant is allowed to process Samsung Pay payments with
Samsung Pay                       decrypted payment data.
decrypted
                                   Note: This option works only if the Can pay with Samsung Pay
                                   option is enabled.


The Samsung Pay settings must be configured on the Di                               gital wallets tab of the merchant
settings.


Acquirer options
The acquirer via which the payment is performed must have the Samsung Pay payment
way enabled in the acquirer configuration.


User permissions

(see "Adding a group of permissions" and “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-Commerce
Payment Gateway: User Guide):

Permission                                                                        Action type        Level

6.37.4.1 Request for Samsung Pay payment with encrypted data
  The /api/v1/samsungpay/payment/encrypted or /api/v1/samsungpay/payment/encrypted-
  anonymous method is used to transfer encrypted data for a Samsung Pay payment.
  The /api/v1/samsungpay/payment/encrypted request is authenticated, in this case the
  userName and password parameters are required for authentication.
  The /api/v1/samsungpay/payment/encrypted-anonymous request is anonymous, in this case
                                (

6.37.5 Request for Yandex Pay payments
  Yandex Pay payments are processed using the /api/v1/yandexpay/payment method. The
  following forms of the request are used :

  · A request with encrypted token (authenticated or anonymous)
  · A request with decrypted token

  System settings
  On the Administration > System settings page of the EPG administration portal the
                                                         (
  following settings must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
  Installation and Configuration Guide):
  yandexpay.gateway.name

  Description                Yandex Pay gateway name.
  yandexpay.offlineSignatureValidationOnly

  Description                Enables or disables offline signature validation:

                             · true — offline signature validation is enabled.
                             · false — offline signature validation is disabled. This is the default
                                value.


  yandexpay.useTestSigningKeys

  Description                Specifies the signing keys that must be used for online validation:

                             · true — the signing keys from
                               https://sandbox.pay.yandex.ru/api/v1/keys/keys.json must be used.
                                This is the default value.

                             · false — the signing keys from
                               https://pay.yandex.ru/api/v1/keys/keys.json must be used.

  yandexpay.notification.connectTimeout.millis

  Description                                                (                      )
                             Connection timeout in milliseconds for notification requests to
                             Yandex Pay. The default value is 10000.
  yandexpay.notification.connectionRequestTimeout.millis




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                     |   261
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




Description                Request connection timeout (in milliseconds) for notification requests
                           to Y andex Pay. The default value is 10000.


yandexpay.notification.readTimeout.millis

Description                Read timeout (in milliseconds) for notification requests to Yandex Pay.
                           The default value is 10000.


yandexpay.notification.kid

Description                Key ID to be sent to Yandex Pay in JWT header “kid”. It is used for
                           authentication purposes in notification requests.


yandexpay.notification.url

Description                URL to which notification requests are sent. The default URL is
                           https://sandbox.pay.yandex.ru/api/psp/v1/payment_notification.

yandexpay.notification.maxAttempts

Description                Maximum number of attempts to resend a notification. The default
                           value is 24.


yandexpay.notification.redeliveryDelay.millis

Description                Notification redelivery delay, in milliseconds. The default value is
                           3600000.

yandexpay.notification.redelivery.retry.db.check.interval.seconds

Description                Frequency of checks for notification redelivery, in seconds. The
                           default interval is 30.

6.37.6 Request for Mir Pay payments
  Mir Pay payments are processed using the /api/v1/mirpay/payment* APIs. The following
  forms of the request are used :

  · A request with encrypted token (authenticated or anonymous)
  · A request with decrypted token

  System settings
  On the Administration > System settings page of the EPG administration portal the
                                                         (
  following settings must be specified see SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
  Installation and Configuration Guide):
  mirpay.nspk.public.key.alias

  Description                NSPK Mir public key alias in the system keystore. The default value is
                             nspkpublickey.


  mirPay.merchantManagementService.url

  Description                Mir Pay Merchant Management Service URL and port.

  mirPay.merchantManagementService.connectionRequestTimeout

  Description                                                            (                   )
                             Connection request timeout in milliseconds for requests sent to the
                             Mir Pay Merchant Management Service. The default value is 5000.

  mirPay.merchantManagementService.socketTimeout

  Description                                        (                       )
                             Socket timeout in milliseconds for requests sent to the Mir Pay
                             Merchant Management Service. The default value is 5000.




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                   | 2 74
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




mirPay.merchantManagementService.connectTimeout

Description                                               (                       )
                           Connection timeout in milliseconds for requests sent to the Mir Pay
                           Merchant Management Service. The default value is 5000.

mirPay.merchantManagementService.maxConnections

Description                Maximum number of connections allowed for requests to the Mir Pay
                           Merchant Management Service. The value must be integer. The
                           default value is 10.


mirPay.merchantManagementService.maxPerRoute

Description                Maximum number of connections allowed for requests to the same
                           route of the Mir Pay Merchant Management Service. The value must
                           be integer. The default value is 2.

paymentToken string. The token format is defined by the MIR System standard П.275: «“Mir
Payment Network Standard. Description of Implementation of In-Application Operations
for Acquirer or Aggregator based on the Mir Pay Android Service”.
Note: The document is available in the Russian language.

encoded fragments separated by a dot: BASE64URL(UTF8(JWE Protected Header)) || '.' ||

   The /api/v1/mirpay/jwks/{certificateName} method is used to request the Mir Pay member

6.38 Managing merchants
  An aggregator is a merchant that has submerchants and processes their transactions. A
  submerchant is a dependent merchant that does not have its own terminal and processes
  its payments through an aggregator.

  A submerchant does not have a Processing ID or Terminal ID. It uses aggregator’s values
  for these parameters.

  In the EPG system, it is possible to manage merchants and submerchants through the UI
  (administrative portal) and through API. The web API enables the creation of a
  submerchant and the modification of its details.



6.38.1 Merchant creation request
  To create a merchant or a submerchant, the create.do method is used.

  A submerchant inherits a range of parameters from the aggregator. If the same
  parameters are specified for the submerchant, their values will be ignored. The inherited
  parameters are: processingId, terminalId, merchantLogin, visa3dsId, masterCard3dsId,
  mir3dsId, currencies, defaultCurrency, paymentAttempts, mustVerify,
  externalFraudControlEnabled, and orderStatusPeriodDays.
  To be able to manage merchants through API, a user must be added in the EPG
  administrative portal to the group that has the VIEW and EDIT actions for the
  EXTERNAL_MERCHANT_MANAGEMENT entity (see “Administration > Groups” in SmartVista E-
  Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide). The user must have the following permissions:
  · Have the Use Merchant API permission enabled (see “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-
    Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).
  · Have the Submerchants management allowed and Use Merchant API permissions enabled to
    be able to manage submerchants through API and                                UI (see “Creating a user” in
    SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).

Name                                                                              Type            Mandatory
Specifies whether a challenge is requested for the transaction. For example, for 01-PA,
a 3DS requestor may have concerns about the transaction, and request a challenge. For
02-NPA, a challenge may be necessary when adding a new card to a wallet.
Possible indicator values:

· 01 — no preference
· 02 — no challenge requested
· 03 — challenge requested: 3DS Requestor Preference
· 04 — challenge requested: Mandate
· 05 – 79 — reserved for EMVCo future use
· 80 – 99 — reserved for DS use

 Note: If the element is not provided, the expected action is that the ACS would
 interpret as 01 — No preference.

6.38.2 Merchant update request
  To update a merchant’s or submerchant’s data, the update.do method is used.

  A submerchant inherits a range of parameters from the aggregator. If the same
  parameters are specified for the submerchant, their values will be ignored. The inherited
  parameters are: processingId, terminalId, merchantLogin, visa3dsId, masterCard3dsId,
  mir3dsId, currencies, defaultCurrency, paymentAttempts, mustVerify,
  externalFraudControlEnabled, and orderStatusPeriodDays.
  To be able to manage merchants through API, a user must be added in the EPG
  administrative portal to the group that has the VIEW and EDIT actions for the
  EXTERNAL_MERCHANT_MANAGEMENT entity (see “Administration > Groups” in SmartVista E-
  Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide). The user must have the following permissions:
  · Have the Use Merchant API permission enabled (see “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-
      Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).
  · Have the Submerchants management allowed and Use Merchant API permissions enabled to
      be able to manage submerchants through API and                              UI (see “Creating a user” in
      SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).

  Request parameters
  Note: Any hyphens displayed in the parameter names below are inserted solely for
  formatting reasons.

6.38.3 Merchant deletion request
  The delete.do method is used to delete a submerchant from the EPG system. Only
                                                (
  submerchants can be deleted not merchants or aggregators .                                 )
  To be able to manage merchants through API, a user must be added in the EPG
  administrative portal to the group that has the VIEW and EDIT actions for the
  EXTERNAL_MERCHANT_MANAGEMENT entity (see “Administration > Groups” in SmartVista E-
  Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide). The user must have the following permissions:
  · Have the Use Merchant API permission enabled (see “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-
    Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).
  · Have the Submerchants management allowed and Use Merchant API permissions enabled to
    be able to manage submerchants through API and                                UI (see “Creating a user” in
    SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide).




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                   |   327
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface

6.39 Managing bindings
 A binding links together in a merchant system the identifier of a customer of the merchant
 (clientId) and the number of the customer card (PAN). A binding is created on a
 successful payment for goods or services (a payment without errors, with the response
 containing "errorCode":"0","errorMessage":"Success").

 If a binding is deleted by the customer, it becomes inactive in the EPG system.
 The following EPG database tables are used for the binding:

 · BINDING — stores bindings
 · BINDING_HISTORY — stores all binding operations (create and update)

 Bindings can be used only if a merchant has the permission to create and manage
 bindings.




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                               |   335
  S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




  The bindingId parameter can be passed to EPG during registration of an order. In that
  case, the order can be paid only with this binding.


  Merchant options
  The following permissions are mandatory for a merchant to manage bindings:

  · Merchant is allowed to use bindings
  · Can create and update bindings without payment

  To create links for bindings, merchants must have at least one of the following
  permissions enabled :

  · Can send a link to the payment/binding form via e-mail
  · Can send a link to the payment/binding form via sms

  For more information about merchant options, see “Main information tab” in the
  “Merchants” section of the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway: User Guide.
  User permissions
  The user must have the following permission enabled on the Administration                              > Users page
  (see “Adding a group of permissions” and “Creating a user” in SmartVista E-Commerce
  Payment Gateway: User Guide):

  Permission                                                                        Action type       Level
  Can create order for binding/update card by the                                   API               Regular user
  link
  Create a link for the card update. This permission enables users to create an order and
  send the link to the binding web page to cardholders.

6.40 P2P methods
 P2P payments are payments that are made when transferring funds from one card to
 another. The card from which funds are transferred is called the source card and can
 belong to either the customer’s bank or a third -party bank. The card to which the funds
 are transferred is called the receiver card and must belong to the customer’s bank.


 Merchant options
 To be able to execute P2P methods, the merchant must have at least one of the
 following permissions enabled depending on the type of P2P transfer being performed
 (also see the p2p_type           460
                                        parameter :   )
 · Can use 'standard' P2P transfers
 · Can use P2P credit operations
 · Can use P2P debit operations




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                          |   379
  S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface

6.40.2 Request for P2P funds transfer
  The p2p/perform and p2p/public/perform methods are used to perform a card -to-card
  money transfer. The p2p/public/perform method is used by third parties integrated with
  EPG via the EPG APIs.

  If the p2p.verify.mandatory setting is set to true, verifying the payment data with the P2P
  transfer verification request is mandatory prior to executing the transfer processing
  request.


  Request parameters
  Name                                                                              Type           Mandatory
  orderId                                                                           ANS36          Yes
  Unique order number generated by EPG after the registration of the order.
  amountInput                                                                       N 1..12        Conditional


  Amount of the transaction. If this field is specified, it overrides the amount specified
  during order registration and will be used instead of that value.

  The value must be specified in the minor denomination of the currency.

   Note: The amount field is required if the p2p.anonymous.amount.change.allowed setting on
   the Administration > System setting s page is set to true. The default setting value is
   false, which means the ability to change the amount is disabled.

6.40.4 Request for P2P transfer verification
  The p2p/verify and            p2p/public/verify requests are used to check whether a P2P
  transfer is possible before ma king the transfer. The p2p/public/verify method is used by
  third parties integrated with EPG via the EPG APIs. In case of a successful response these
  requests return the transfer fee details.

  This request relates to the following system settings configured on the Administration                           >
  System settings page of the EPG administration portal:
  · p2p.verify.mandatory — when this setting is set to true, the transfer verification request
    must be called to check the data of a P2P money transfer before executing the transfer
    processing request.

  · 3ds2.amount.includeFees — when this setting is set to true, it enables including the
    transaction fee in the purchaseAmount field of the AReq message (for the 3-D Secure 2
    protocol .   )
  · 3ds.amount.includeExternalFees — when this setting is set to true, it enables including
                                                                 (
    the fee provided by the external source for example, an O TP system in the               L       )
    authorization request amount for both protocols 3-                           D Secure 1 (PaReq) and 3-D Secure 2
    (AReq).
  · p2p.anonymous.amount.change.allowed — when this setting is set to false, it disables
    changing the transaction amount for the following P2P methods: perform.do or
                                          ;
    verify.do for the web API performP2P or verifyP2P for the SOAP API. After the
    transaction verification request is executed, the amount cannot be changed regardless
    of this setting.




  Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                 |   404

original request:

· Scheme
· ServerNam
· ServerPor

  finishPageLogin was not specified)
· /finish.html with an appended orderId
· lang (for transactions with the specified language)
· status (for transactions with the transaction state).

Depending on the transaction result, the URL is as follows:
· The failUrl value if it was specified or (if there is no failUrl) the returnUrl value with
   an appended orderId parameter, if the Show finish payment page option is disabled for
   the merchant.

· The failUrl value if it was specified or (if there is no failUrl) the returnUrl, but without
  an appended orderId parameter if the request attributes are presented and they are

6.41 QR payment methods
  Merchants can accept QR payments performed via a QR provider system such as Fast
         ( )
  Payments SPB .

  ATTENTION: To work with the FastPayment API, check that the sslKeyStoreFile and
  sslKeyStorePassword system parameters are configured and the required FastPayment
  certificates and keys are added to the keystore. For more information, see the
  “Configuring a keystore” section in the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
  Installation and Configuration Guide.
  The following database tables are used for QR payment transactions:

  · MERCHANT_FASTPAYMENT_CONFIG — stores information used to generate requests to the
      FastPayment (SBP) API
  · QR_TRANSACTIONS — stores basic information about QR transactions
  · FAST_PAYMENT_TRANSACTION_DATA — stores payment information

  Note: A merchant must have the Can use QR Fast Payments (SPB) permission to process
  QR payments made via the Fast Payments system. For more information, see “Main
  information tab ” in the “Merchants” section of SmartVista E-Commerce Payment Gateway:
  User Guide.

6.43.2 Creating a binding (saving the card for a non-payment
transaction)
  A binding is created as follows:

  1. A merchant registers an order (registerBindingOrder.do) with the following parameter:
      o bindingManagedByMerchant = true — bindings are managed by the merchant and EPG
        is requested not to save the bindings in the system.

  2. The merchant’s system initiates the processBindingOrder.do request.
  3. When authorization is completed, EPG responds to the merchant and passes
     transactionData:
      o In a response to the paymentOrder.do request only for SSL and Frictionless
        transactions.

      o Always in a response to the getOrderStatus.do (getOrderStatusExtended.do) request.
  Notes: The createBindingNoPayment.do method is never used for the PCI DSS merchants.
  The transactionData data must be saved by the merchant if bindingManagedByMerchant =
  true. If bindingManagedByMerchant = false, a merchant can ignore transactionData.


6.43.3 CIT payments with a binding

  certified with PC I       DSS:
  · Saving a card during payment or paying with a binding

  · Initial recurring/installment payment (CIT)

Transaction Data block
A single signed data block is used to transfer all original transaction data fields to and
from a PC I     DSS merchant, instead of multiple separate fields.
An RSA key pair with CertificateType.TRANSACTION_DATA_SIGNATURE must be generated for
the merchant.

   · The key provided in the JWS header cannot be found for the current merchant.
   · Signature validation fails (both technical and not errors).

6.43.4.2 Creating a recurring payment template
   To create a template for the recurring payment without saving the card details to EPG:

   1. A merchant initiates the createRecurringTemplateNoPayment.do request with
      recurringPaymentManagedByMerchant = true.
   2. When authorization is completed, EPG responds to the merchant and passes the
      transactionData block:
       o In a response to the paymentOrder.do request only for SSL and Frictionless
         transactions.

       o Always in a response to the getOrderStatus.do (getOrderStatusExtended.do) request.

6.43.4.3 Subsequent recurring/installment payment (MIT)
                                       (                )
   A subsequent recurring installment payment is performed as follows:

   1. A merchant registers an order with the following parameters:
       o recurringPaymentForm — either recurring (for recurring payments) or installment (for
         installment payments              )
       o recurringExpiry — specified optionally
       o recurringPaymentManagedByMerchant = true — recurring payments are stored and
         managed by merchants

       o transactionInitiator = MIT — transaction is initiated by the merchant
       o originalTransactionData that the merchant has received when performed the CIT
         transaction.

       o originalInstallmentNumber — specified if recurringPaymentForm = installment
   2. The merchant’s system triggers the paymentOrder.do request.
   3. When authorization is completed, EPG responds to the merchant and passes the
      transactionData block:
       o In a response to the paymentOrder.do request only for SSL and Frictionless
         transactions.

       o Always in a response to the getOrderStatus.do (getOrderStatusExtended.do) request.
   Note: The transactionData must be saved by the merchant if bindingManagedByMerchant =
   true.




   Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                               |   454
  S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




6.43.4.4 No-Show payment
  Note that merchants must save customer’s card credentials using any available method.
  After that, they will receive the transactionData block in a response. For example:

  · Creating a binding (saving the card for a non-payment transaction)
                                                                                             449




  · Saving a card during payment or paying with a binding

  No-Show payments are performed as follows:
  1. A merchant registers an order with the following additional parameter:
      o bindingManagedByMerchant = true — bindings are managed by the merchant and EPG
        is requested not to save the bindings in the system.

      o transactionInitiator = MIT — transaction is initiated by the merchant.
      o bindingUsage = paymentBySavedCard — card stored during the previous transactions is
        used in the next transaction

      o originalTransactionData that the merchant has received when performed the CIT
        transaction.

     Note: The originalTransactionData value is validated by EPG only if
     bindingManagedByMerchant = true.

  2. The merchant’s system triggers the paymentOrder.do request with noShowPayment = true.
  3. When authorization is completed, EPG responds to the merchant and passes the
     transactionData block:
      o In a response to the paymentOrder.do request only for SSL and Frictionless
        transactions.

      o Always in a response to the getOrderStatus.do (getOrderStatusExtended.do) request.
   Note: The transactionData must be saved by the merchant if bindingManagedByMerchant =
   true.

7 Merchant callback APIs
 This section describes callback requests sent by EPG to merchants.

 A callback is sent via the HTTP protocol using the GET or the POST method. The address to
 which the callback is sent is specified by the Callback address parameter in the merchant
 properties.

 If the callback is processed by the recipient successfully, EPG receives the HTTP code
 200. If the completion code is not successful, repeated requests are sent until the
 ma ximum limit specified by the merchant.callback.maxAttempts parameter on the EPG
 System settings page is reached.
 A callback contains the following data ta ken from the transaction parameters:

 · status — the status assigned to the transaction after this operation:
     o Successful transaction — status = 1, Action code = 0
     o Unsuccessful transaction — status = 0, Action code = value other than 0.
 · operation — the last status of the transaction:
     o deposited
     o approved
     o reversed
     o refunded
     o declined
 · Other parameters as specified by the merchant.callback.availableFields parameter on
                      gs (see the “Merchant callback settings” section in the SmartVista
   the EPG System settin
   E-Commerce Payment Gateway: Installation and Configuration Guide). This parameter is
   configured at the system level for all merchants registered in EPG.


 A set of additional parameters can also be specified for a specific merchant by the
 Additional parameters to send setting in the merchant configuration (for more
 information, see the “Notifications tab ” section in the SmartVista E-Commerce Payment
 Gateway: User Guide).
 The following additional parameters can be specified :

     o amount
     o feeAmount
     o authorizationResponseId
     o approvedAmount
     o bankName
     o currency
     o currentState
     o date




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                               | 45 6
S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




    o depositedAmount
    o depositFlag
    o eci
    o fraud
    o ip
    o ipCountryCode
    o maskedPan
    o mdOrder
    o merchantFullName
    o merchantLogin
    o orderDescription
    o orderNumber
    o panCountryCode
    o paymentDate

    o paymentState

    o processingId

The authorization field of the request header will contain a cryptogram if the following
parameters are configured and the corresponding key is added to the keystore:

· Alias of merchant JWT key for callback operation — this parameter is configured at the
  merchant level.

· jwt.keystore.path, jwt.keystore.password,merchant.callback.jwt.key.password              — these
  parameters are configured at the system level.


If these parameters are not configured or configured incorrectly, the callback is sent
without the authorization header.

8.4 Customizing payment methods
 A method for processing a customer’s payment is defined by the paymentWay parameter of
               (
 a request a registration, preauthorization registration request, or a request for an
                                           )
 alternative payment method . The parameter value is selected from a predefined list of
 values that reflects available payment methods:

 · CARD — payment made by entering the card details
 · CARD_BINDING — payment made using a binding
 · CARD_MOTO — payment made using the call center
 · UPOP_MOTO (CUP UPOP MOTO) — payment made China UnionPay Express Pay
 · UPOP — payment made China UnionPay Secure Pay
 · FILE_BINDING — payment made using a binding uploaded in a file
 · P2P — payment made when transferring funds from one card to another
 · APPLE_PAY — payment made using the Apple Pay service
 · MASTERPASS — payment made using a Masterpass e-wallet
 · OTHER — payment used for orders processed outside EPG
 · GOOGLE_PAY — payment made using the Google Pay service
 · SAMSUNG_PAY — payment made using the Samsung Pay service
 · NSPK_E_CERT — payment made using the NSPK Electronic Certificate
 · FASTPAYMENT_QR — payment made using the FastPayment QR code
 · MPU — payment via Myanmar Payment Union (MPU)
 · WAVE — payment via WavePay

 If you want to use custom payment methods (for example, a bank transfer), the following
 configuration must be applied :




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                 | 49 5
 S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface




 · The paymentWay parameter that is passed as a separate parameter in a request must be
   set to Alternative (OTHER).

 ·

  Note: During the registration of a payment, specifying the payment method is not
  mandatory but it must be specified at payment completion. If it is not specified, the
  appropriate payment method is automatically defined by EPG.

8.6 Specifying reccurenceFrequency
 The Quartz cron is used to configure the recurring payments frequency. More information
 is available at the following             URL: http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-
 2.2.2/tutorials/crontrigger.html.
 The value format is <* * * * * *>           — a line consisting of six required time and date fields and
 one optional field separated by a white space. The fields are as follows:


  Field position Unit of                                       Allowed values               Allowed special
                           measurement                                                      characters
  First                    Seconds                             0-59                         , - * /

  Second                   Minutes                             0-59                         , - * /

  Third                    Hours                               0-23                         , - * /

  Fourth                   Day-of-month                        1-31                         , - * ? / L W

  Fifths                   Month                               1-12 or JAN-DEC              , - * /

  Sixth                    Day-of-Week                         1-7 or SUN-SAT               , - * ? / L #

  Seventh                  Year (Optional)                     empty, 1970-2199             , - * /
  (optional)




 Confidential © 2025 BPC Banking Technologies                                                                 | 502
 S martV ista E-Commerce Payment Gateway 202504.4: S pecification – A PI: RES T Interface
